title: Beef and Pepper Briouats with Lemon-Garlic Dip
summary: Crisp fried filo triangles packed with a spiced filling of beef, peppers, onion and parsley, served hot with a cool lemon-garlic mayonnaise dip.
equipment: deep frying pan or wide pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, water, lemon juice, garlic and cumin until smooth, then chill. Resting lets the garlic flavour spread through the dip.

steps.title: Onion
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the onion, cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until soft. Uncover and cook for 3-5 minutes more, until the liquid has gone; a dry base keeps the pastry crisp.

steps.title: Peppers
steps.text: Add both peppers, the parsley, paprika, cumin, coriander, salt and cayenne and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until the peppers are soft. Cooking the spices in the fat brings out their aroma.

steps.title: Beef
steps.text: Add the beef and cook for 4-5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains, the pan is dry and it reads 71 °C. Spread it out to cool to room temperature and tip away any pooled fat.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Stack the filo and cut it into strips about 15 x 28 cm. Keep them covered with a damp towel, as filo dries out and cracks within minutes.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold one strip in half lengthways to make a 7.5 cm wide strip. Put a heaped tablespoon (about 20 g) of filling near the bottom, fold a corner over it to make a triangle and keep folding the triangle up the strip. Trim any extra pastry, set it seam-side down and repeat to make 16.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 1.5 cm oil in a deep frying pan to 180 °C. Fry in batches, seam-side down first, for 2-3 minutes in total, turning once, until golden and crisp on both sides. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the dip.

tips: Oil that is not hot enough is the usual mistake: the pastry soaks up oil. Check it is at 180 °C before each batch.
Fold tightly so no filling can escape into the oil.
Folded briouats can be frozen on a tray, then fried from frozen for an extra minute.
Keep finished batches warm in a low oven.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best fried and eaten fresh. Cooked briouats keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat at 200 °C for 6-8 minutes until piping hot (74 °C). The dip keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
